name: Koilwar Bridge
facts: Koilwar Bridge, officially Abdul Bari Bridge, opened on 4 November 1862, becoming the oldest operational railway bridge in India and the longest river bridge in the subcontinent until 1900.
Designed by James Meadows Rendel and Sir Matthew Digby Wyatt, the 1.44‑km steel lattice girder bridge was inaugurated by Viceroy Lord Elgin, who praised it as only second to one bridge worldwide.
The bridge’s twin road lanes, part of Old NH 30, run beneath the rail tracks, linking Arrah on the west bank to Bihta, Danapur, and Patna across the Sone River.
